cs.t: I really like this setup: iPad +  Korg microKEY-37 + KORG Gadget 3 + all a bunch of KORG apps No subscriptions. Keyboard is wireless but no noticeable latency. In my workflow I pretty much never need more keys but if I do I just use a MIDI adapter and plug a larger keyboard. KORG apps go on 50% sale several times every year.
cs.th: Apple introduces the new iPad Air, powered by M4

cs.t: Korg microkey is great; I have stacked two of them on my other keyboard and use it even for live setups without any issue so far; see e.g.  https://www.youtube.com/shorts/S82hsEDY8Pc  or  http://rochus-keller.ch/?p=1153 .
cs.th: Ask HN: What MIDI micro/nano keyboard(s) do you like? (Electronic music)

cs.t: The Korg Microkey 61 got me through university. It was the only MIDI keyboard I could find with a small form factor + ... a lot of keys. I used it with a NanoKontrol 2 to get some knobs/faders. After graduating, I got myself a weighted 88-key MIDI keyboard so I could properly play piano, but some of my favorite 'music memories' are riffing on those bouncy mini keys.
